_doc: THE CONFUSION LEDGER (Ian, 2026-09-14: 'even you sometimes confused like the sign in, that is why we have to have more trajectories, targeting that makes you confused, and work our way to improve it. it is the same way improving our UFAI UI UX platform wide' - and, asked whether that meant sign-in: 'I am not referring to signing in only, I am referring to any other kinds and types'). Every point of ANY kind where a WALK - an agent driving the platform as a person - hesitated, mis-clicked, picked the wrong control, waited without knowing, lost its place, hit a dead end, landed somewhere else than it meant to, or read a sentence it could not act on is written here the day it happens, and tools/seed_expansion_wave4.py --add-confusions turns each entry into one W4 trajectory per axis (kind 'confusion'): lived start to end, fixed, re-walked, locked. What confuses the agent confuses a person; the ledger is the UFAI improvement backlog in its rawest form. Append-only; an entry is never deleted, only marked fixed with its verification. Two kinds are also MEASURED automatically on every step by tools/phone_fit_audit.mjs (`ambiguity`, `unactionable`); the rest are read from the walk.

kinds.ambiguity: two or more controls announce the same name for different jobs (the wall's two 'Sign In'); measured per step
kinds.wait-without-knowing: a state that takes long with nothing said about why, how long, or what to do (25 s of 'Signing in…')
kinds.unactionable-sentence: an error, status or alert in the transport's or the developer's words, not the person's ('name resolution failed'); measured per step
kinds.silent-scope: a view, filter or mode that quietly narrows what a search or list shows ('No tools match' inside Engineer view)
kinds.lost-place: focus or scroll position lost after a close, a save, a repaint (focus on <body> after every overlay closes)
kinds.look-alike-controls: two controls that look and read alike but do different things (a search button and a filter input)
kinds.silent-failure: something breaks and only the console knows (the _tt ReferenceError on every mode click)
kinds.dead-end: a state with no way onward or back (an empty state with no next step)
kinds.wrong-arrival: the person lands somewhere other than where they meant to (a return= that does not return, a deep link that drops its target)
kinds.hidden-by-chrome: a control the person cannot reach because chrome covers it (the FAB over Save); measured per step as occlusion
kinds.chrome-stands-down: the shell disappears behind a dialog and the person cannot tell whether it is gone or hidden (the hub invisible behind the sign-in wall)
kinds.off-screen: a control clipped by the viewport edge, hidden by no chrome (assistant's New Chat running 21px past 320); measured per step as element overflow
kinds.wrapped-label: a one-line control's label breaks onto two lines at a narrow width (a tab strip whose items may shrink); measured per step as wrapped
kinds.small-target: a control a person can see but not reliably hit: narrower or shorter than the platform's 44px floor at the viewport it was met on

A person using a screen reader hears the same name twice; the walker's role locator resolved both and could not choose. The page behind an open modal is not inert, so the opener stays in the accessibility tree while the dialog is up.

entries.walk: W41384 ratchet (prove_w4_navhub.mjs) - assistant.html, cast as Christine Dizon, at 'hub closed'
entries.confusion: A signed-in worker lands STRAIGHT on assistant's chat screen (the page skips setup when a session exists), whose header carries the page's own 'Setup' back button top-left (button.flex @16,60 63x44). wayfinding.js did not recognize assistant's handleBack() buttons (they had no .back-link/.back-btn class) and injected its FIXED back-pill (#wh-wayfinding) on top - elementFromPoint at the Setup button's centre returned #wh-wayfinding. THIRD occurrence of the chrome-over-control class (after pm-scheduler's Save and the offline banner over wf-back), and the first where the covering chrome is a DUPLICATE back control the platform added on top of the page's OWN back control; worse under the offline banner, which slides the pill down onto the button. A plain worker who lands on setup first never sees it - persona/route-dependent, caught because the ratchet casts the row's own hive member who is already signed in.
entries.improvement: A page that manages its OWN back affordance (a multi-screen SPA like assistant, whose two screens each ship a handleBack() button) marks those buttons with class 'back-link', which wayfinding.js already treats as the SKIP path - it returns without injecting the pill AND without rewiring, so handleBack survives - and which the W1/L rubric credits as an in-layout way back. The general rule: an owned back affordance opts OUT of the injected pill by wearing a class wayfinding recognizes, so the platform never stacks a second back control on the page's own.
entries.status: fixed + verified on the real page 2026-09-14: the serial single-host re-walk of assistant.html (W41384, cast Christine Dizon) read 0 findings, 11/11 controls, and the row is banked to locking. entries.improvement: A page's sticky bottom CTA must leave the shared FAB band clear at narrow widths - reserve the FAB's column (right padding/max-width on the bar) or lift the FAB stack above the bar by the bar's height (publish --wh-sticky-cta-h the way the offline banner publishes its height), so the nav launcher is always reachable.
entries.status: RETRACTED as an occlusion 2026-09-14 (a walk artifact, kept for the record): #wh-hub is z-index 9998, far above the bar's 40, so the bar cannot cover a LIVE fab. The fab was absent from the fabStack because the walk was still on the SIGN-IN WALL with the modal up - nav-hub.js hides #wh-hub (visibility:hidden) while an overlay is open, by design (the chrome-stands-down rule), and the bar simply occupies that spot. Root cause was the WALKER: a fixed 2s sleep then a textbox count read 0 at 320 on this loaded host (the modal opens later under RAM pressure), so sign-in was never attempted, the gated host bounced back to the wall, and index.html was graded as the host (idKept false). Fixed in w4_navhub_walk.body.js: wait up to 15s for the username box before deciding there is no wall. The ONE real finding on that wall - the bar's 'Get Early Access: It's Free' label wrapping to 2 lines in its 216px column at 320 - is fixed in index.html (one size step down + nowrap below 360px). Lesson: read a fabStack as a z-order snapshot at a moment, and ask WHICH page the walk is actually on before naming a coverer.

With the companion or feedback panel open, the notice sits over what they are reading or typing.
entries.improvement: A notice never covers something interactive: _whShowNotice measures the fixed bottom chrome already on the page (learn chip, sticky CTA, hub fab, open panels) and places itself above the tallest of them, and an open companion/feedback panel raises the notice above its own body; nothing a person can tap sits under a notice at rest or with a panel open.
entries.status: fixed BOTH HALVES (2026-09-16, sw v417) - verified live through the Playwright MCP at phone-390 on the shipped shell. FIRST HALF (v394, 2026-09-15, unchanged and still holding): the notice raises itself above the page-guide chip, data-wh-bottom 203px. SECOND HALF (v417): the notice now YIELDS to an overlay that covers it. Measured before: notice 532..643 (z 2147483000) over #wh-fb-body 522..622 inside #wh-feedback-panel 0..844 (z 9999) - overlaps true. Placement could never fix that: clearing an 844px full-height panel needs bottom >= 844, past the 60% cap (506px) the placement deliberately refuses to cross, so this was a z-order problem and the z-index is itself correct (a stale-version message must outrank page CONTENT, just not a panel opened a second ago). Measured after: panel open -> notice display none, height 0; panel closed via its own 'Close feedback panel' button -> display block, height 111. The fix tests INTERSECTION, not mere presence, so a popover elsewhere does not silence the message; it ignores display:none / visibility:hidden / zero-opacity / under-8px overlays because a CLOSED off-canvas panel keeps its box; and its 500ms re-check is created with the notice and cleared by the same 30s cleanup, so no page carries a timer for a message that is gone. BOTH occlusions cleared with the one change - span.wh-notice-ref (the companion finding) lives inside the notice, so hiding it took that too, which is why the re-walk went 2 findings -> 0. RE-WALKED AND BANKED: dayplanner.html through the Playwright MCP, 24 records, withFindings 0, 11/11 controls, 0 problems, identity kept across all 4 pages; W41393 banked locking/60 on instrument playwright-mcp, PASS trajectory-registry. FOUND ONLY BECAUSE THE GATE LEARNED TO LOOK: bank_mcp_navhub_walk.py summed the 4 at-rest page arrivals and never opened <id>.records.json, the ~24 interaction records where the panels are actually opened - a page at rest is the one state where a panel cannot be covering anything. It now reads them and refuses a row while an interactive state carries an occlusion. W41367 and W41368 still carry an uncounted 'feedback open from the hub' finding from before the fix and want a re-walk.
entries.fix: utils.js _whShowNotice (precached SHELL, sw v393->v394): the bottom-chrome measurement that decides the notice's height ran ONCE at show time, and the page-guide chip (learn-link.js) paints on its own 300 ms..12 s schedule after the update notice fires, so the notice stayed at its literal 160px over the chip. The placement is now a function called at show time and again at 0.5/1.5/3/6/12.5 s while the notice is up; it only ever raises the notice (data-wh-bottom keeps the high-water mark) and the chip's own avoidance list deliberately excludes notices, so there is one mover. Also: the notice's Retry/Reload/Sign-in button 32 -> 44px. Teeth: prove_w4_confusions.mjs C28 (gate w4-confusions).

entries.fix: wh-feedback-fab.js .wh-fb-panel max-width 100vw -> 100%. Mechanism found with the MCP (containing-block probe): innerWidth 390 but documentElement.clientWidth 384 - the browser draws a 6px classic scrollbar; 100vw includes it, a fixed box's right:0 does not, so a 390px-wide panel anchored at 384 starts at -6. A phone with overlay scrollbars never shows it; any desktop window narrower than 380px with a classic bar does. Network-first file, no sw bump.
